<lead_handoff>
Research task (read-only, no repo changes). Goal: collect primary-source evidence about how leading coding-agent harnesses design their model-facing tool set, so I can decide how OpenPI should restructure its dynamic tool loading. Context: OpenPI (repo ~/work/openpi-latest-main) is a Pi extension package. It keeps an initially tiny tool set and dynamically loads "capability groups" (search: fd/rg/git_show/git_diff/git_log; delegate: subagent_*; workflow; background: bg_*; session: tasks_*/goal; runtime_snapshot) by prompt keywords plus mid-session setActiveTools toggles. This mid-session tool churn breaks prompt cache (issue #879). We are considering freezing the tool set and deleting low-value tools.

For EACH harness below, report facts with a source link (GitHub file path at a specific commit/tag, or official doc URL) and a short verbatim quote or code excerpt for each claim. Prefer reading actual source over blogs. Harnesses:
1. OpenCode (sst/opencode, or anomalyco/opencode): full built-in tool list; whether tools are static per session; how MCP tools are added; any tool search/deferred loading; todo/task tool; subagent (task) tool; background process tools; how they handle prompt caching (cache_control placement, system prompt stability).
2. OpenAI Codex CLI (openai/codex, Rust): built-in tool list (shell, apply_patch, update_plan, view_image, etc.); whether tool set changes mid-session; MCP handling; any tool_search / deferred tools; prompt cache key usage.
3. Claude Code: built-in tool list from official docs (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, Task/Agent, TodoWrite, BashOutput/KillShell, WebFetch, etc.); MCP Tool Search / defer_loading behavior and the threshold when it kicks in; anything about prompt caching and tool stability.
4. A DeepSeek-oriented harness: search for what exists (e.g. DeepSeek official agent/CLI, "deepseek-tui", "DeepSeek harness"); report what you find and its tool design. If nothing official exists, say so.
5. Kimi CLI (MoonshotAI/kimi-cli) and Goose (block/goose): tool list and dynamic-loading behavior, briefly.
6. Manus "Context Engineering for AI Agents" blog: the exact guidance on KV-cache, masking vs removing tools.
7. Anthropic docs: tool search tool / defer_loading, and the prompt-caching doc statement on what invalidates cache (tools changes). OpenAI docs: prompt caching + allowed_tools / tool_choice guidance.

Also, for OpenCode and Codex specifically: how do they implement "background/long-running commands" (separate tools vs a flag on the shell tool), "file search" (dedicated glob/grep tools vs just shell), and "todo" (always-present tool vs conditional)?

Output: write findings to /tmp/openpi-harness-research.md, organized per harness, every claim with link + quote; mark anything you could not verify as UNVERIFIED. End with a compact comparison table: harness | #built-in tools | static per session? | background exec design | search tools | todo tool | subagent tool | MCP/large catalog strategy. Do not make recommendations for OpenPI. Report back the file path and a brief summary.
</lead_handoff>

# Web Search Results for "Claude Code MCP tool search defer_loading threshold tools"

## 1. Scale to many tools with tool search - Claude Code Docs
URL: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search

Tool search is on by default, with the exceptions listed in Configure tool search. When it is active, tool definitions are withheld from the context window. The agent receives a summary of available tools and searches for relevant ones when the task requires a capability not already loaded. Up to five of the most relevant tools are loaded into context by default, where they stay available for subsequent turns until the SDK compacts the messages where the agent discovered them. After that compaction, the agent searches for those tools again when it next needs them. Tool search adds one extra round-trip each time Claude searches for tools, but for large tool sets this is offset by smaller context on every turn. With fewer than ~10 tools whose definitions fit comfortably in the context window, loading everything upfront is typically faster. For details on the underlying API mechanism, see Tool search in the API.

  if (cache?.type !== "ephemeral" && cache?.type !== "persistent") return undefined
  if (breakpoints.remaining <= 0) {
    breakpoints.dropped += 1
    return undefined
  }
  breakpoints.remaining -= 1
  return Cache.ttlBucket(cache.ttlSeconds) === "1h" ? EPHEMERAL_1H : EPHEMERAL_5M

import { FileDiff } from "@opencode/schema/file-diff"
import { createTwoFilesPatch, diffLines } from "diff"

export function fileDiff(
  file: string,
  before: string,
  after: string,
  status: typeof FileDiff.Info.Type.status = "modified",
): typeof FileDiff.Info.Type {
  const counts = diffLines(before, after).reduce(
    (result, item) => ({
      additions: result.additions + (item.added ? (item.count ?? 0) : 0),
      deletions: result.deletions + (item.removed ? (item.count ?? 0) : 0),
    }),
    { additions: 0, deletions: 0 },
  )
  return {
    file,
    patch: createTwoFilesPatch(file, file, before, after),
    status,
    ...counts,
  }
}

---
title: Tool search tool
url: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool
description: Scale to hundreds or thousands of tools by letting Claude search your tool catalog and load only the tools it needs.
---

The tool search tool lets Claude work with hundreds or thousands of tools by discovering and loading them on demand. Instead of loading all tool definitions into the context window up front, Claude searches your tool catalog (including tool names, descriptions, argument names, and argument descriptions) and loads only the tools it needs.

Loading every tool definition up front causes two problems as a tool library grows:

* **Context bloat:** A typical multiserver setup (GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana, and Splunk) can consume \~55k tokens in definitions before Claude does any work. Tool search typically reduces this by over 85 percent, loading only the 3–5 tools Claude needs for a given request.

# How Claude Code uses prompt caching

> Claude Code manages prompt caching automatically. See why a model switch triggers a slow uncached turn, what `/compact` costs, why CLAUDE.md edits don't apply mid-session, and how to check your cache hit rate.

Prompt caching makes Claude Code faster and more cost-efficient. Without caching, the API would reprocess your full history on every turn. With caching, it reuses what it already processed, bills the re-read at the [cached token rate](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing), and fully processes only what changed.

Claude Code handles prompt caching for you, unless you [disable it](#disable-prompt-caching). It is still useful to know how prompt caching works, because some actions invalidate the cache and make the next response slower and more expensive while it rebuilds. # Web Content from https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching

# Prompt caching

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to the page URL.

## Why prompt caching matters

Prompt caching reuses work when requests share the same prompt prefix. This provides three main benefits:

- **Compute-efficient:** Avoid recalculating a prompt prefix that the model has already processed.
- **Cheaper input tokens:** Pay the model's reduced cached-input rate for reused tokens, discounted up to 95%.
- **Faster:** Reduce the time spent processing input before the response starts.

Prompt caching is enabled by default for supported OpenAI models. Use the [Prompt Caching Dashboard](https://platform.openai.com/usage?usage_section=prompt-caching) to monitor cache read hit rates and use the [Prompt Cache Diagnostics tool](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching/diagnostics) to diagnose cache misses and improve cache reuse.

    pub async fn list_tools(
        &self,
        session_id: &str,
        extension_name: Option<String>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Tool>> {
        let include_final_output = extension_name.is_none();
        let lease = self.extension_manager.current_lease(session_id).await?;
        let mut prefixed_tools = match extension_name {
            Some(name) => lease.tools_for(&name).await,
            None => lease.tools().await,
        };

        if include_final_output {
            let final_output_tool = self
                .config
                .session_manager
                .get_session(session_id, false)
                .await
                .and_then(|session| ops_recipe::final_output_tool(&session));
            if let Ok(Some(final_output_tool)) = final_output_tool {
                prefixed_tools.push(final_output_tool.tool());
            }
        }

        Ok(prefixed_tools)
    }

Tool search allows the model to dynamically search for and load tools into the model's context as needed. This allows you to avoid loading all tool definitions into the model's context up front and **may help reduce overall token usage and cost**. # Agent Note: Tool schemas are part of the system-prompt assembly

Status: implemented
Archived: 2026-07-27

English | [中文](2026-06-11-tool-schemas-in-prompt-assembly.zh.md)

## Problem

On the wire, tool schemas travel in a dedicated `tools` field of the model request, not in prompt text. Architecturally, though, "what the model is told it can do" is one coherent concern: prompt sections and the tool list are assembled from the same plugin contributions and consumed at the same moment.

## Decision

`PromptAssembly { sections, tools }`: the system-prompt service collects ordered text sections AND tool schemas (the tool registry auto-contributes a provider). The loop consumes one assembly per step; adapters map `sections` to the provider's system slot and `tools` to the wire `tools` field. The `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall is therefore a single interception point for everything the model is told up front — tool filtering (ToolSearch / progressive disclosure) is an assembly rewrite, same as prompt edits.

**The loop queries the tool registry separately from the prompt service** — splits one coherent concern across

## Headline findings

**The industry converged on: freeze the wire `tools` list; deliver changes as appended context; mask rather than remove.**

- **OpenCode** (`dev` @ `8c173a8`, now a v2 Effect-based rewrite): model sees only 12 `codemode: false` native tools + one `execute` CodeMode meta-tool. *All* MCP tools and internal tools go into a CodeMode catalog rendered as **instructions** (~2k-token inline budget, overflow discoverable via an in-runtime `search()` function). Catalog changes are **appended as diff messages** ("The Code Mode tool catalog has changed…"), keeping the prefix intact. It keeps tool defs on the final step with `toolChoice: "none"` explicitly "to preserve the provider's cached prefix", and sets a per-session `promptCacheKey`. Shell has a `background: true` flag; there is **no todo tool**.
- **Codex CLI** (`main` @ `ce0323f`): much bigger than the classic 4-tool set — a `ToolRegistry` with per-tool `ToolExposure` (Direct/Deferred/CodeModeOnly/Hidden). Deferred MCP tools go on the wire with `defer_loading: true`; a BM25 `tool_search` tool materializes them "for the next model call". Mid-session catalog changes produce appended developer notices (added/removed/schema_changed). `prompt_cache_key` = session id. No glob/grep tools — `rg` via `exec_command`; background = PTY session id + `write_stdin`; `update_plan` is config-gated.
- **Claude Code** (docs): ~40 documented tools but highly conditional — Glob/Grep are **absent by default on macOS/Linux/WSL** (model uses `find`/`grep` via Bash); `TodoWrite` is disabled by default and the `Task*` family is model-gated; `ToolSearch` + `WaitForMcpServers` are conditional. Tool search (default on supported models, `auto` = 10%-of-context threshold) means "Claude Code keeps the tool list from the conversation's first request for the whole conversation" — MCP connect/disconnect then can't disturb the cache.
- **DeepSeek `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` (`dsh`)** — an official harness exists. Best direct precedent: its plan-mode prompt states *"The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability… those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged"* — it masks mutation tools via prompt text rather than changing the tool list. Also has a `run_code` code-mode presentation preset.
- **Kimi CLI**: static 17-tool YAML roster per agent; dedicated `TaskList/TaskOutput/TaskStop` bg tools; plan mode enforced by edit-time rejection, not removal; MCP tools appended on background connect.
- **Goose**: the outlier — `manage_extensions`/`search_available_extensions` let the model enable/disable extensions mid-session and the tool list is rebuilt per request (i.e., it does churn `tools`).
- **Provider mechanics**: Anthropic — "Modifying tool definitions… invalidates the entire cache"; deferred tools are excluded from the prefix and `tool_reference` blocks are expanded inline so "the prefix is untouched, so prompt caching is preserved"; `tool_addition` beta adds tools mid-conversation without touching `tools`. OpenAI — `tools` changes affect the cached prefix; tool search injects discovered tools "at the end of the context window"; `allowed_tools` tool_choice masks without mutating `tools`.
- **Manus blog**: exact guidance captured — "avoid dynamically adding or removing tools mid-iteration" (KV-cache invalidation + model confusion over dangling references); mask via logit/state machine; name-prefix conventions (`browser_`, `shell_`) for stateless masking.

The file ends with the requested comparison table (harness | #built-in tools | static? | background exec | search tools | todo | subagent | catalog strategy) plus a cross-cutting pattern summary — no OpenPI recommendations, per the brief.

- Goose's prompt-caching internals and Codex per-model feature-flag defaults are marked UNVERIFIED.
- Sources were cloned to `/tmp/opencode-repo` and `/tmp/codex-repo` if you want to grep further.

主 Pi Session 始终拥有用户交互、配置和生命周期。Terminal、Subagent 与 Workflow 是三条执行路径；Tasks、Goal、Session 和 Context Pivot 保持连续性；Footer、Dashboard、Artifacts 与清理逻辑负责观察和控制。

### 一项任务应该去哪里？

ˋˋˋtext
长期进程                         → Background Terminal
一项自包含、可继续对话的委派     → Subagent
多阶段、依赖、fan-out 与综合      → Workflow
跨回合工作项                     → Tasks
持续自主目标                     → Goal
同一 Session 的阶段切换          → Context Pivot
真正跨顶层 Session               → 独立 pi-intercom package（按需安装）
ˋˋˋ

 "old_string": "Capability discovery 默认是 `explicit`：普通父 Session 不常驻任何 OpenPI 模型工具，首轮保持 Pi 原生 `read`、`bash`、`edit`、`write`。用户明确要求结构化搜索、Subagent、Workflow、后台进程或 Session Goal/Tasks 时，OpenPI 在 `before_agent_start` 直接加载对应能力组；明确询问 OpenPI capabilities/tools/features 时显示 `openpi_load_tools`。可通过 `/openpi-setup` 显式选择 `adaptive`：此时只让小型 `openpi_load_tools` 网关常驻，模型可在判断任务确实受益时自主加载一个能力组。该选择也授权模型启动该组内的昂贵工作，因此不作为默认值。句首「子代理了解下项目」这类带执行动作的表达会加载 Delegate；「子代理是什么」这类讨论、否定表达和条件句（例如 “If you delegate…”）不会被当成显式委派意图。能力组在当前 Session 内单调保持，避免反复增删工具破坏缓存。Delegate 一经加载便一次性开放完整、稳定的 Subagent 工具族；资源不存在时由工具执行层明确返回空状态或 fail-closed，而不再按实例生命周期改变模型接口。其他组内管理工具仍只在资源成功创建或状态确实存在后出现。Mode / Setup / Context 工具独立跟随实时状态显示和隐藏。Background、Subagent 与 Workflow 的 Skill 文件仍随包发布，但只在对应能力触发后提示读取，不常驻普通系统 Prompt。\n\n只读诊断可通过现有网关 `openpi_load_tools({groups:[\"runtime\"]})` 按需加载 `runtime_snapshot({})`；不会因提示关键词自动加载，也不会常驻普通工具面。它仅对父 Session 开放，区分有效配置、Session 当前选择、磁盘 Git 状态和已注册扩展；无法证明的 loaded revision、版本或上游路由明确为 unknown/unavailable。模型标识、路径、账号、endpoint 与资源标题不输出；保留默认模型匹配结果、thinking、实时 Trust、允许公开的工具名与资源状态。整个工具结果上限 16 KiB，跨 owner 最多 32 项，非原子采样、不可用和省略量均显式标记；不启动资源、不消费模型、不写配置。详见 [运行时快照边界](docs/architecture/RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT.md)。",
 "new_string": "OpenPI 提供一套固定的常驻模型工具，在 Session 开始时确定一次：Subagent（`subagent_spawn` 等 6 个）、Workflow（`workflow`/`workflow_stop`/`workflow_status`）、后台终端（`bg_start` 等 5 个）与 Goal（`create_goal`/`get_goal`/`update_goal`）。会话内工具列表不因模型动作或运行时状态改变；缺少对应状态的调用（如无终端时的 `bg_status`、无目标时的 `update_goal`）在执行层返回明确结果或 fail-closed。只有用户显式边界会改变工具：`/plan` 加入只读 Git、`plan_ready` 与 `ask_user`/`human_handoff`；`/openpi-setup` episode 加入 `configure_my_pi_setup` 与 `ask_user`/`human_handoff`；浏览器授权后启用 `openpi_browser`。Background、Subagent 与 Workflow 的 Skill 文件仍随包发布，模型按需用 `read` 读取，不常驻普通系统 Prompt。"
}

## Lifecycle and replay

Interactive TUI runs return an accepted run id immediately by default, release the parent turn, and later deliver a terminal completion with a stable delivery id. Delivery is at least once: normal retries do not duplicate a run, but a process loss after Pi accepts the message and before the receipt is persisted can replay the same id. `wait: true` explicitly waits inline; interrupting that wait releases only the waiter and the run continues. /** Return the leading system message, if the transcript starts with one. */
export function getInitialSystemMessage(messages) {
    const first = messages[0];
    return first && isSystemMessage(first) ? first : undefined;
}
/** Drop the leading system message for APIs that carry the prompt outside the message list. */
export function withoutInitialSystemMessage(messages) {
    return getInitialSystemMessage(messages) ? messages.slice(1) : messages;
}
/** Resolve the tools available after applying every transcript delta in order. */
export function getCurrentTools(messages) {
    const tools = new Map();
    for (const message of messages) {
        if (!isSystemMessage(message))
            continue;
        for (const tool of message.toolsRemoved ?? [])
            tools.delete(tool.name);
        for (const tool of message.toolsAdded ?? [])
            tools.set(tool.name, tool);
    }
    return [...tools.values()];
}

- Byte-identical frozen-surface integration test passes: provider-request `tools` arrays (names + serialized schemas) and system prompts identical across `session_start`, a `bg_start` turn, `create_goal`→clear, and large-context `agent_start`; `/plan` adds exactly `git_show/git_diff/git_log/plan_ready/ask_user/human_handoff` once and leaving restores the original list exactly.

## What I fixed this session (test adaptation tail)

16 failing tests after the source migration, all stale expectations — no production bugs found:

- `tests/extensions/plan-mode/index.test.ts` — mock now captures `pi.on` handlers and fires `session_start` (with a `sessionManager.getBranch()` stub) so the boundary reconcile runs before asserting `plan_ready` is hidden.
- `tests/extensions/setup/index.test.ts` — dropped `Capability discovery`/`adaptive` assertions from the two setup-prompt tests (feature removed).
- `tests/extensions/background-terminals/index.test.ts` — both tests now assert all 5 `bg_*` tools resident at session start and unchanged by rejected/successful starts.
- `tests/extensions/git-read/call-rendering.test.ts` — mock `pi` gained an `events` stub for the new `PLAN_MODE_CHANNEL` subscription.
- `tests/extensions/goal/index.test.ts` — three tests rewritten for resident goal tools; added an assertion that `get_goal` with no goal throws `No goal is currently set.` at execution time.
- `tests/extensions/subagents/agent-types.test.ts` — `VALID` fixture now uses `[read, grep, find, ls]`; added a focused test that `fd`/`rg`/`tasks_add` produce "no longer provided by OpenPI and is ignored" diagnostics.
- `tests/extensions/subagents/prompt.test.ts` — `rg` fixtures swapped to `grep`.
- `tests/extensions/suggestions/config.test.ts` — removed `capabilities: {discovery}` from config-shape and status-line expectations.
- `tests/web/provider-settings-page.spec.ts` — removed the deleted `capabilityDiscovery` combobox block; the setup-routing assertion now runs through `workflowConcurrency`.

## Environment note (was a blocker)

`node_modules` was stale relative to `bun.lock`: `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` requires `highlight.js@10.7.3` nested (its deep import `highlight.js/lib/core.js` is blocked by v11's exports map), and the nested copy was missing, so *every* test crashed with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` on both Node 26 and 22. `bun install` fixed the tree. Also note: system `node` is v26; the repo's suite was run with `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22` (engines ≥22.19).

## Status summary

- 79 working-tree entries: 54 files in `git diff --stat` (+906/−1326), plus deletions of `extensions/{capabilities,context-pivot,file-search,runtime-snapshot,tasks}/`, `extensions/shared/capability-intent.ts`, and their tests; `file-search/src/{output,process}.ts` renamed into `git-read/src/`.
- `web/dist/app.js` rebuilt and tracked — consistent with `bun run check`'s build.

## Deviations / uncertainties

- `OPENPI_TOOL_SURFACE.plan.boundary` enables `plan_ready` for the whole plan episode including ready state; execution rejects when a plan is already ready — preserves the old hidden-tool semantics as required.

- Historical docs (`docs/design/TASKS_EVALUATION.md`, `BLOG_SESSION_TASKS_DESIGN.md`, `docs/research/WEB_SUBAGENTS_2026-10-13.md`) still mention deleted tools, but they're dated records and `AGENTS.md` forbids silently rewriting legacy documents; the two architecture/decision docs describing current behavior (`RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT.md`, `0004-capability-name-discovery.md`) got superseded/removed status headers instead.

 87|> [!TIP]
 88|> OpenPI 为每个 Session 提供一套固定的常驻模型工具：`subagent_spawn`/`subagent_wait`/`subagent_cancel`/`subagent_send`/`subagent_check`/`subagent_list`、`workflow`/`workflow_stop`/`workflow_status`、`bg_start`/`bg_status`/`bg_list`/`bg_kill`/`bg_watch`，以及 `create_goal`/`get_goal`/`update_goal`。该列表在 Session 开始时确定一次，之后不因 Prompt 关键词、目标状态或后台进程变化而改变——常驻工具面是缓存稳定的，也是模型可预期的。
 89|> 只有明确的用户边界会临时增减工具：进入 `/plan` 加入 `git_show`/`git_diff`/`git_log`、`plan_ready`、`ask_user`/`human_handoff`，退出时移除；`/openpi-setup` 进行期间提供 `configure_my_pi_setup` 与 `ask_user`/`human_handoff`；浏览器控制经 Setup 授权后启用 `openpi_browser`。缺少对应状态的工具调用（例如没有 Goal 时调用 `update_goal`）在执行层返回明确错误，而不是隐藏工具。

## Regression fix (C1)
2. Child tools are `inheritedChildToolAllowlist(parentActive, roleTools)` = parent ACTIVE ∩ role tools (extensions/shared/child-session.ts ~636-660; called from subagents/index.ts ~1081 and workflows ~1768). Parent sessions don't activate Pi's `grep`/`find`/`ls`, and `git_*` are active only during /plan, so explorer/read-only/planning children end up with only `read` (+git_* in plan). Before this branch, /plan loaded fd/rg into the parent so planning children could search. Fix in that shared function only: when `roleTools` is defined (explicit role list or plan-mode child list), names in a new exported constant `CHILD_READ_DERIVED_TOOL_NAMES = ["grep", "find", "ls", ...CHILD_SAFE_PACKAGE_TOOL_NAMES]` that the role explicitly lists are allowed even if not active in the parent, **provided the parent has `read` active** (they are read-only inspection already within the parent's read authority). They must still pass the existing `available` provenance check and `isBlocked` policy, and CHILD_EXCLUDED/retired filtering. Order: keep parent-active order first, then append derived names in role-list order. No change when `roleTools` is undefined. Add a short doc comment stating the authority rationale. Tests (extend existing child-session tests, cheapest layer): (a) parent active [read, bash, edit, write] + role [read, grep, find, ls, git_show, git_diff, git_log] → child gets all of those that are available; (b) parent without `read` → derived names NOT granted; (c) a derived name whose provenance is blocked/unavailable still behaves as today (throw/blocked); (d) role undefined → unchanged. Also confirm via one existing subagent spawn-path test (or extend one) that a planning child gets grep/find/git_* from a parent with only read/bash/edit/write + plan boundary tools.

## 配置与参考

Web 模型配置先填写提供商连接，再选择“获取可用模型”。列表支持搜索、勾选当前结果和批量添加，已有配置不会重复添加；搜索保留其他结果的勾选。查询仅请求提供商模型目录，不调用模型。可使用同一已保存端点的 Pi 凭据，或输入仅用于本次查询的临时密钥；临时密钥不会保存。新增模型沿用表单里的能力默认值，可在高级参数中逐项调整。提供商不支持目录接口时仍可手动添加。

Web 侧栏宽度默认 340px（配置兼容范围 220–520px），工具面板宽度默认 520px（360–720px）。拖动或键盘调整后保存到同一份配置，刷新后恢复；小窗口按当前视口临时限制显示宽度，不覆盖已保存值。也可用 `/openpi-setup` 修改 `ui.webSidebarWidth` 和 `ui.webAuxiliaryWidth`。

## 连续工作，而不是堆 Context

test("preview observes cancellation and rejects a file changed during scanning", async (t) => {
  const fixture = await writeSession([
    header(),
    message("m1", null, "user", "x".repeat(2 * 1024 * 1024)),
  ]);
  t.after(() => rm(fixture.directory, { recursive: true, force: true }));

  const controller = new AbortController();
  controller.abort();
  await assert.rejects(
    loadSessionPreviewData(fixture.path, { signal: controller.signal }),
    {
      name: "AbortError",
    },
  );

  let changed = false;
  await assert.rejects(
    loadSessionPreviewData(fixture.path, {
      onRead: () => {
        if (changed) return;
        changed = true;
        appendFileSync(fixture.path, " \n");

export function selectNodeTestShard(files, shard) {
  const match = /^([1-9]\d*)\/([1-9]\d*)$/.exec(shard);
  const index = Number(match?.[1]);
  const total = Number(match?.[2]);
  if (
    !Number.isSafeInteger(index) ||
    !Number.isSafeInteger(total) ||
    index > total ||
    total > files.length
  ) {
    throw new Error(
      "Invalid Node test shard: expected index/total with no empty shards.",
    );
  }
  return files.filter((_, fileIndex) => fileIndex % total === index - 1);
}

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>为什么同时提供 Subagent 和 Workflow？</strong></summary>

Subagent 是一项可继续对话的自包含委派；Workflow 是多阶段编排，强调 fan-out、结构化结果、恢复、验收与持久产物。前者可以接管继续，后者更适合自动化流水线。

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Plan Mode 为什么允许 git log，却拒绝 npm install？</strong></summary>

Plan Mode 不猜“任意 Shell 是否只读”，只放行由已知安全零件组成的命令。不会生成 diff 的窄白名单 Git / GitHub 查询（例如原始 `git log`、`git status`、`git blame`）可以通过；Shell 元字符、未知 flag、安装、写入和无法证明的形式全部拒绝。

进入或恢复 Plan Mode 时，OpenPI 会为当前 Session 加载 `search` 组。差异检查使用结构化 `git_diff` / `git_show`，历史浏览使用 `git_log`；前两者固定传入 `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color`。原始 Bash `git diff`、`git show`、`git whatchanged`，以及 `git log -p`、`--stat`、`--name-only`、`-L` 等会生成 diff 的形式会被拒绝，避免仓库的 `diff.external` 或 textconv driver 执行外部程序。

这项保证精确覆盖 Git diff driver 边界，并不宣称任意 hostile Git 配置都无副作用；其余允许的 Git 调研命令仍位于 Pi 已有的项目 Trust 边界内。

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>后台服务会不会变成孤儿进程？</strong></summary>

正常的 `/new`、`/resume`、`/fork`、`/reload` 与退出都会触发 Session Shutdown。扩展会终止后台进程树并清理临时日志；也可随时用 `bg_kill` 或 `/ps` 管理。

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>这是稳定 API 吗？</strong></summary>

这是持续实际使用的独立发行版，不承诺扩展 API 永远不变。改动会经过 TypeScript、格式检查与专项测试；Pi 上游变化

105:OpenPI ships one fixed, resident model tool set: Subagent, Workflow, and background-terminal tools are active from the start of every Session and do not change with model actions or runtime state. function workflowAgentActivity(runId: string, source: WorkflowAgentSource) {
  const id = `${runId}:call:${source.index}`;
  if (
    !/^wf_[0-9a-f]+$/i.test(runId) ||
    !Number.isSafeInteger(source.index) ||
    source.index === undefined ||
    source.index < 1 ||
    id.length > WEB_MAX_CAPABILITY_ID
  )
    return undefined;
  const title = boundedActivityText(source.label ?? `Agent ${source.index}`);
  const status = workflowAgentStatus(source);
  const outcome =
    status === "done"
      ? ("completed" as const)
      : status === "error"
        ? (source.completion?.observed.outcome ?? source.executionOutcome) ===
          "cancelled"
          ? ("interrupted" as const)
          : ("failed" as const)
        : undefined;
  const item: WebWorkflowAgentActivity = {
    id,
    runId,
    title: title.value,
    status,
    ...(outcome ? { outcome } : {}),
    createdAt: source.startedAt ?? 0,
    ...(source.finishedAt !== undefined
      ? { settledAt: source.finishedAt }
      : {}),
    ...(source.replayed !== undefined ? { replayed: source.replayed } : {}),
  };
  return { item, truncated: title.truncated };
}

export function bashReceipt(content: unknown, isError: unknown) {
  if (isError !== true) return undefined;
  const lastPart = Array.isArray(content) ? content.at(-1) : undefined;
  const value = typeof content === "string" ? content : evidenceRecord(lastPart).type === "text" ? evidenceRecord(lastPart).text : undefined;
  if (typeof value !== "string") return undefined;
  const last = value.slice(-512).trimEnd().split("\n").at(-1);
  if (last === "Command aborted") return { state: "cancelled" as const };
  if (/^Command timed out after \d+(?:\.\d+)? seconds$/u.test(last ?? "")) return { state: "timed_out" as const };
  const exit = /^Command exited with code (-?\d+)$/u.exec(last ?? "");
  if (exit && Number.isSafeInteger(Number(exit[1]))) return { state: "failed" as const, exitCode: Number(exit[1]) };
  return undefined;
}

}

function canonicalStatus(value: unknown): Status {
  if (value === "running") return "running";
  if (value === "done" || value === "completed") return "done";
  if (
    ["error", "failed", "aborted", "killed", "timed_out"].includes(
      String(value),
    )
  ) {
    return "error";
  }
  if (value === "uncertain") return "warn";
  return "unknown";
}

function resultStatus(
  message?: WebLiveMessage,
  liveState?: EvidenceState,
): Status {
  if (message?.forkSnapshotToolResult) return "unknown";
  if (liveState === "running") return "running";
  if (liveState === "unknown") return "unknown";
  if (!message) return "unknown";
  if (message.isError) return "error";
  const status = canonicalStatus(record(message.details).status);
  if (status !== "unknown") return status;
  return message.isError === false ? "done" : "unknown";
}

ˋˋˋ

Pi will load the extensions and theme the next time it starts. OpenPI's Background, Subagent, and Workflow Skill files remain in the package, and the model reads them through Pi's native skill mechanism when needed; ordinary turns do not inline them in the system prompt.

The terminal theme above remains Pi-owned. OpenPI Web has separate package-owned appearance preferences: `system`, `light`, and `dark` modes; chat width from 820-2000px; chat font size from 12-24px; and whether thinking blocks start expanded. `system`, 820px, 14px, and collapsed are the defaults. The complete `ui.webAppearance` object defaults to `{ "palette": "default", "accent": "", "background": "", "foreground": "", "font": "codex" }`. Palettes are `default`, `mist`, `rose`, and `pine`; fonts are `codex` (Codex default), `sans`, `serif`, and `mono`. Legacy `system` maps to `codex` when reading configuration or importing a theme.   if (result?.forkSnapshotToolResult) return { state: "unknown" as const };

function resultStatus(
  message?: WebLiveMessage,
  liveState?: EvidenceState,
): Status {
  if (message?.forkSnapshotToolResult) return "unknown";
  if (liveState === "running") return "running";
  if (liveState === "unknown") return "unknown";
  if (!message) return "unknown";
  if (message.isError) return "error";
  const status = canonicalStatus(record(message.details).status);
  if (status !== "unknown") return status;
  return message.isError === false ? "done" : "unknown";
}

Read-only research task (no edits to any repo). Goal: collect source-level evidence of how Codex, OpenCode and Apache Maka implement specific agent-harness mechanisms, so I can compare against OpenPI/Pi. Local clones: /tmp/codex-repo (openai/codex @ce0323f), /tmp/opencode-repo (sst/opencode dev @8c173a8), /tmp/maka-src (apache/maka @d14cec5). Use them; `git -C <repo> log -1` for the commit. For EVERY claim give file path + line range + a short verbatim excerpt. Mark anything not found as NOT FOUND (do not guess). Keep each answer factual; no recommendations.

Topics (answer per harness):
1. **Tool-output size control & context pruning**: per-tool output truncation limits (bytes/lines/tokens); whether older tool results are pruned/elided/summarized before later model calls; exact trigger thresholds; WHEN the rewrite happens (only for the newest result before it is first sent, or retroactively on history already sent) — this matters for prompt-cache prefix stability. Maka: the "context-budget tool-result prune" (active + stale, 2048 estimated tokens) — find the implementation. OpenCode: compaction/prune of tool parts. Codex: output truncation + auto-compaction.
2. **Compaction**: trigger (token threshold / context %), what is kept, whether it is model-summarized, how the cache prefix is treated afterwards.
3. **Shell & background processes**: Codex unified exec (PTY session id, yield_time_ms, write_stdin, max sessions, cleanup on exit); Maka Bash + WriteStdin + StopBackgroundTask; OpenCode shell `background` flag. For each: what happens to still-running processes when a non-interactive run ends (killed vs left alive)?
4. **Non-interactive / headless mode**: Codex `exec`, OpenCode `run`, Maka headless hosted execution: which tools and what system prompt are used vs interactive; any different behavior (approval, completion criteria, final message).
5. **Edit tool design**: apply_patch vs search/replace edit; how failures are reported to the model (e.g. fuzzy matching, line hints).
6. **Prompt caching mechanics**: where cache breakpoints / prompt_cache_key are set; how they keep the prefix stable (tool ordering, system prompt stability, dynamic content placement such as date/cwd/env).
7. **Subagents**: tool list and default-on status; how results return to the parent (blocking vs async notification); concurrency limits; whether children share the parent's cache key.
8. **System prompt size**: approximate size (chars) of the default interactive system prompt / base instructions and where it lives.

Write findings to /tmp/harness-research-2.md organized by topic then harness, ending with a compact comparison table per topic. Report back the path and a <=15-line summary.

pub(crate) async fn build_compaction_replacement_history(
    sess: &Session,
    step_context: &StepContext,
    world_state: &WorldState,
    compacted_history: Vec<ResponseItemEnvelope>,
) -> (Vec<ResponseItemEnvelope>, WorldStateSnapshot) {

        .await;
    let (prefix, context) = split_prefix_updates(updates);
    let context = merge_world_state_updates(context);
    (
        assemble_compaction_history(compacted_history, prefix, context),
        snapshot,
    )
}

/// Format the combined exec output for sending back to the model.
/// Includes exit code and duration metadata; truncates large bodies safely.
pub fn format_exec_output_for_model(
    exec_output: &ExecToolCallOutput,
    truncation_policy: TruncationPolicy,
) -> String {
    // round to 1 decimal place
    let duration_seconds = ((exec_output.duration.as_secs_f32()) * 10.0).round() / 10.0;

    let content = build_content_with_timeout(exec_output);

    let total_lines = content.lines().count();

    let formatted_output = truncate_text(&content, truncation_policy);

    let mut sections = Vec::new();

    sections.push(format!("Exit code: {}", exec_output.exit_code));
    sections.push(format!("Wall time: {duration_seconds} seconds"));
    if total_lines != formatted_output.lines().count() {
        sections.push(format!("Total output lines: {total_lines}"));
    }

    sections.push("Output:".to_string());
    sections.push(formatted_output);

    sections.join("\n")
}

const truncateToolOutput = (value: string) => {
  if (value.length <= TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS) return value

  // Count code points so a surrogate pair is never split.
  let end = 0
  let kept = 0
  for (const char of value) {
    if (kept === TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS) break
    end += char.length
    kept++
  }
  if (end === value.length) return value
  return `${value.slice(0, end)}\n[truncated]`
}

 * Why Runtime Host refused to open a Turn for an explicit Skill invocation.

 * than in a payload nothing reads.
 */
export function skillInvocationBlockedMessage(skillInvocation: SkillInvocationResult): string {

      : `/skill:${failure.request} (${failure.reason.replaceAll('_', ' ')})`,
  );
  return reasons.length > 0
    ? `Could not resolve the Skill this Turn asked for: ${reasons.join(', ')}`
    : 'Explicit Skill invocation could not be resolved';
}

Done. Written to **`/tmp/harness-research-2.md`** (37.7KB, 542 lines) — organized by topic → harness with file:line + verbatim excerpts, a per-topic comparison table, and NOT FOUND markers where evidence was absent.

**Summary:**

- **Tool-output pruning**: Codex middle-truncates each result to 10k tokens at production/record time; OpenCode caps at 2,000 lines/50KiB at production with the full body saved to a file. **Maka uniquely rewrites history retroactively**: before every send, any function_response whose effective projection >7,500 bytes (~2k est. tokens) is archived (sha256/ledger) and replaced by a `maka.archived_tool_result` placeholder with a `page` preview + `resourceRef` + "Use Read with the next parameters to continue" — reasons `stale_tool_result_pruned_before_compact` / `active_current_turn_tool_result_pruned_before_next_step` map exactly to the "active + stale" mechanism you described. Prefix churn is handled via projection-transition digest/currency checks.
- **Compaction**: Codex = token-limit or ctx-window% trigger, model or remote-v2 summary, keeps user messages + summary. OpenCode = est ≥ window−10% (16k reserve), keep newest user messages within 15k tokens verbatim, `<conversation-checkpoint>` format, plus provider-native compaction. Maka = provider-accepted baseline + reply-reserve ≥ user-declared window only; durable validated checkpoints.
- **Background processes**: Codex kills all unified-exec processes at session shutdown; Maka kills them at session close ('shutdown') — both match OpenPI's old behavior. OpenCode keeps them alive via job recovery + auto-notification on completion.
- **Caching**: Codex `prompt_cache_key`=session_id with named drift detection (`tools_changed`…); OpenCode auto-breakpoints (last tool + first/last system + tail, ≤4) with "most→least shared" instruction ordering and appended (never rewritten) date/env updates; Maka `maka:<sessionId>` + single Anthropic breakpoint at the replayed-history boundary, dynamic context always appended after it.
- **Subagents**: all three keep children as separate sessions/cache chains. Maka's `tool_search` is the interesting parallel to pre-#879 OpenPI — deferred loading, but activations are append-only per session. Maka Code Mode defaults to `direct` (off).

## Delete the workspace cleanup guard entirely (user decision)
Evidence: native Pi has no deletion guard. In the 2026-10-18 Terminal-Bench runs the guard blocked legitimate commands in nginx-request-logging and regex-log in both rounds — compound commands like `cd /app && rm -f test_regex.py && ls …`, and even standalone `rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default` — forcing extra model turns; in no-UI sessions Pi's `confirm` always returns false (pi-coding-agent dist/core/extensions/runner.js:134), so pre-existing deletions can never be approved. Peers do not block-and-retry in non-interactive runs (Codex exec approvals Never; OpenCode run auto-rejects with feedback).

<lead_handoff>

## Problem (settled — your Probe B confirmed it)
extensions/plan-mode/index.ts:690-724: the `context` hook appends a transient `openpi-plan-context` custom message at the TAIL of every provider request once any `my-pi-setup-plan-mode-state` entry exists in the branch (including status "inactive"). The next request inserts new messages before it, so request k is never a prefix of request k+1. Pi's anthropic-messages provider puts its only history cache breakpoint on the last user message, and Anthropic only writes cache entries at the breakpoint, so after one /plan use every later request re-writes the whole history and never reads it. Peers fix this by putting the state reminder in history once, at the transition (OpenCode packages/core/src/plugin/plan.ts; Codex world_state diffs).

## Design (decided — implement exactly this)
Keep the `context` hook as the single source of plan reminders (it already handles /tree navigation, compaction, old sessions, malformed state), but make the projection append-only and position-stable instead of tail-appended:

1. Walk `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` and collect every `custom` entry with customType PLAN_MODE_STATE_ENTRY, in order. For each, derive its reminder text purely from that entry's own `data` (never from runtime vars), so the text for an old entry never changes:
   - planning → BLOCK_REASON
   - ready → the existing ready text ("The plan is ready. All tools remain blocked …")
   - inactive → the existing inactive text ("Current Session state: Plan mode is inactive. …")
   - malformed/undecodable → BLOCK_REASON (fail closed, matching restorePlanModeState). Reuse/export decodePlanModeState from persisted-state.ts rather than duplicating decoding.
   Skip an entry whose derived text equals the previously projected entry's text (consecutive duplicate states).
2. Anchor each reminder at the entry's position in time: insert it into event.messages immediately before the first message whose `timestamp` (ms) is strictly greater than Date.parse(entry.timestamp). If none, append at the end (it will stay there as the stable anchor until later messages arrive — those have larger timestamps and land after it). Then, if the insertion index points at a `toolResult` message, advance past the consecutive run of toolResults, so a reminder can never sit between an assistant tool call and its results (this happens when plan_ready commits state mid-turn). Insert in branch order so multiple reminders keep their relative order.
3. Still strip any pre-existing `openpi-plan-context` messages from event.messages first (as today). Keep `display: false`; use a deterministic `timestamp` for the injected message (e.g. the entry's parsed ms) — it must be identical across requests.
4. Keep the early return when the branch has no plan-state entry (zero overhead for sessions that never used /plan). Drop the old `if (!planning)` runtime branch; the branch is the source of truth. Update the comment above the hook (it currently says "without persisting a message"); describe the stable-anchor rationale in one or two lines (cache prefix stability). Don't touch other comments.

Assert every consecutive pair of captured request message lists is an exact prefix (JSON-equal), and the inactive reminder text appears exactly once. ### Assistant

Committed locally as **`d94e17f7`** on `feat/frozen-tool-surface` (`fix(plan-mode): keep plan reminders prefix-stable for prompt caching (#879)`), 3 files, +350/−34. Not pushed; working tree clean. Probe artifacts remain at `/tmp/probe/`.

## Implementation

`extensions/plan-mode/index.ts` — the `context` hook rewritten exactly as designed:
- Walks `getBranch()` collecting `PLAN_MODE_STATE_ENTRY` custom entries in order; derives text per entry via the newly-exported `decodePlanModeState` (planning/malformed → `BLOCK_REASON`, ready → ready text, inactive → inactive text — both texts extracted unchanged as `READY_PLAN_CONTEXT`/`INACTIVE_PLAN_CONTEXT`); consecutive duplicate texts skipped; runtime `planning`/`readyPlan` vars no longer consulted.
- Each reminder inserts before the first `event.messages` entry whose `timestamp` (ms) is strictly > `Date.parse(entry.timestamp)`; absent/unparseable timestamps anchor at the end. If the index lands on a `toolResult`, it advances past the run so a mid-turn `plan_ready` commit never splits a tool call from its results. Injected `timestamp` = the entry's parsed ms (deterministic), `display: false`, pre-existing `openpi-plan-context` messages still stripped first. Early return preserved when the branch has no state entries.

## Tests

New `tests/extensions/plan-mode/context-projection.test.ts` (3 tests):
- **Real-session prefix test** — faux-provider fixture with only plan-mode loaded; `{status:"inactive"}` entry appended like `commitPlanState`, two prompts with an intervening `read` tool call; asserts every consecutive request pair is an exact JSON prefix, the reminder appears exactly once per request, and its position is identical across all requests.
- **Anchoring/ordering** — planning/dup-planning/ready entries at controlled timestamps: exactly 2 reminders (dedup works), correct texts, planning reminder before the assistant tool call, ready reminder after the toolResult (the split-prevention path exercised), deterministic timestamps, idempotent re-projection.
- **Malformed entry** — decodes to `BLOCK_REASON` at its anchor (fail-closed preserved).

No existing test needed updating — `control.test.ts` assertions (all text-presence + idempotence checks) pass unchanged; none asserted tail position.

## Problem
In `pi -p` / `--mode json`, Pi's print mode calls session.prompt() and then disposes the runtime and exits (node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/modes/print-mode.js:103-143). A subagent still running when the parent turn ends is stopped and its result never delivered. The subagent_spawn tool result (buildSubagentSpawnResult in extensions/subagents/src/prompt.ts:208-245) tells the model to end its turn and rely on automatic delivery "in an interactive session", and to use subagent_wait only if "a non-interactive automation must return it" — but nothing tells the model which mode it is in. Workflows already handle this at runtime (extensions/workflows/index.ts:1386 `canDeliverLater = ctx.hasUI && ctx.mode === "tui"` → wait by default).

## Change (decided)
1. buildSubagentSpawnResult gets a new option `exitsAfterTurn?: boolean`. When true, replace the "It runs in the background — keep working… Use subagent_wait… only if…" sentences with exactly:
   `It runs in the background. This is a non-interactive run: the process exits when your turn ends, which stops any running subagent and discards its result. Before your final answer, call subagent_wait(ids: ["${id}"]) for every result you need; subagent_cancel stops it, subagent_check peeks at a running one or lists all.`
   When false/absent, the text is byte-identical to today.
2. At the subagent_spawn call site(s) in extensions/subagents/index.ts, pass `exitsAfterTurn: ctx.mode === "print" || ctx.mode === "json"` (ExtensionMode is "tui" | "rpc" | "json" | "print"; rpc keeps the process alive, so it is not included). Check whether any other path builds the spawn result (e.g. btw/other origins) and pass the same fact there.
3. Do not change tool descriptions/schemas (the resident budget must not move) or subagent_wait's description.

## Tests
- In the existing test file that covers buildSubagentSpawnResult text (find it under tests/extensions/subagents/), add: exitsAfterTurn=true contains "non-interactive run" and the subagent_wait call with the id, and does NOT contain "automatically re-invoked"; default stays unchanged (assert the old sentence is still present).
- If an existing test drives subagent_spawn's execute with a ctx carrying `mode`, add one case with mode "print" asserting the new guidance appears in the tool result; if no such harness exists, don't build one — say so.

 "content": "# OpenPI 使用细节参考\n\n本文是 [README.md](README.md)（[中文](README.zh-CN.md)）的详细参考，集中保留各能力的行为细节与边界说明。入门介绍与快速开始见 README。\n\n## OpenPI 解决什么\n\nPi 的价值在于小：Agent loop、工具、Session 与扩展 API 已经足够。真实项目缺的不是另一套平台，而是围绕这些原语的一层可靠运行时。\n\n| 开发现场                                | OpenPI 的处理方式                                                            | 保留的边界                         |\n| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |\n| Dev server、watcher、长测试占住主 Agent | Pi 的 Bash 直接后台运行长期进程（如 `nohup … &`）                          | 进程属于本机环境，Session 不托管   |\n| 调研、实现、审查互相污染 Context        | 每个 Subagent 使用独立的进程内 Pi SDK Session                                | Child 不能递归编排或拿回父级工具   |\n| 多阶段 fan-out 靠 Prompt 约定           | Workflow 提供 pipeline、schema、handoff、验收与持久产物                      | Sandbox 不暴露文件、网络或进程 API |\n| 重跑昂贵，却不能信任旧结果              | 只 Replay 在可观测边界内证明为只读且指纹未变的调用                           | 不确定就真实执行，不猜             |\n| 长任务跨回合后失去方向                  | Plan Mode 管理只读调研与实施批准                                            | 它记录与控制，不伪造执行事实       |\n| 并行运行看不见、停不住                  | Footer、Dashboard、Artifacts 与完成通知统一展示状态                          | 每类运行都有检查、取消与唯一终态   |\n\n**核心原则：增强 Pi 的深度，不扩大隐式权限。** OpenPI 沿用用户已有的 Provider、模型、Skills、Trust 与 Session；Suggestion 只有用户开启后才运行，Subagent / Workflow 只在明确的任务动作后运行——主 Agent 调用对应工具，或用户在交互 TUI 中执行 `/btw`——不会因安装或启动自行消费模型。\n\n## 执行约定\n\n执行沿用 Pi 的 Bash 合同：`timeout` 可选且没有统一默认值，是否设置以及设置多长由模型或用户按命令语义决定。OpenPI 不再通过正则改写测试命令 timeout；确实需要有界执行时应显式传入 timeout。长期运行的 build、test、migration 或 server 由 Bash 直接后台运行，例如 `nohup npm run dev &`。\n\n## Subagent 细节\n\n### Pi-native Subagent：隔离 Context，不另起系统\n\nˋˋˋtext\nsubagent_spawn({\n  agent_type: \"explorer\",\n  name: \"audit auth flow\",\n  prompt: \"Trace src/auth end to end and report file:line evidence.\"\n})\nˋˋˋ\n\n每个 Subagent 都是新的进程内 Pi SDK 
… [truncated 31048 chars]

## User

<lead_handoff>
Implement a default bash timeout for non-interactive OpenPI sessions, in ~/work/openpi-latest-main (currently on `main` at 49b2ca34, clean tree). Read AGENTS.md first and follow it. Work on a new local branch `feat/noninteractive-bash-timeout`. Commit locally; do NOT push.

## Why
Peers bound foreground shell commands (OpenCode 120 s, Maka 120 s, Hermes 180 s); Pi's bash has no default timeout. In our benchmarks a model-written script hung bash until the 900 s task deadline. In print/json runs and in subagent/workflow child sessions nobody can press Esc, and those lifecycles are owned by OpenPI (AGENTS.md: the runtime owns time limits). Interactive (tui) and rpc sessions must keep native Pi behavior.

## Settled design (do not change the interface)
New extension `extensions/bash-timeout/index.ts` (default-export `function (pi: ExtensionAPI)`, follow the style of small extensions such as `extensions/turn-time/index.ts`):
- `export const DEFAULT_BASH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120;`
- `pi.on("tool_call", (event, ctx) => …)`: when `event.toolName === "bash"`, `(ctx.mode === "print" || ctx.mode === "json")`, and `event.input.timeout === undefined`, set `event.input.timeout = DEFAULT_BASH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` in place (Pi documents `event.input` as mutable) and remember `event.toolCallId` in a Set. Never touch a timeout the model passed. Do not handle `powershell` (it has no timeout parameter).
- `pi.on("tool_result", (event) => …)`: if `event.toolCallId` is in the Set, delete it; if additionally `event.isError` and the result text contains `Command timed out after ${DEFAULT_BASH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS} seconds` (Pi bash's exact timeout message, see the installed `dist/core/tools/bash.js` around line 275), return `{ content: [...event.content, { type: "text", text: NOTE }] }`. Keep `isError`. Otherwise return nothing.
- NOTE text, verbatim (exported const `BASH_TIMEOUT_NOTE`):
  `OpenPI applied its default 120-second limit because this non-interactive run called bash without a timeout. If the command legitimately needs longer, run it again with a larger timeout (in seconds); start long-running services in the background with nohup … &.`
- No setup option, no config, no system-prompt or tool-definition change (cache-stable; the note only appears in the failing result).
- Child sessions: children run `bindExtensions({ mode: "print" })` (`extensions/shared/child-session.ts:809`) and load package extensions except git-info and parent-only packages (`createChildResources`), so the extension applies there automatically. Do NOT add it to any parent-only list.
- Wire it up wherever the repo registers/lists extensions (package manifest, packaging/file-list tests, smoke tests — find them; e.g. `rg -n "turn-time" --glob '!**/node_modules/**'` shows every place a small extension is listed).

## Tests (follow existing test layout/framework for extensions; keep them small)
1. print mode + no timeout → `input.timeout === 120`; json mode same.
2. print mode + model-supplied timeout (e.g. 5) → unchanged.
3. tui and rpc modes → unchanged (no injection).
4. tool_result: injected call whose error text contains the timeout message → NOTE appended, isError preserved; a call where the model supplied the timeout and timed out → no NOTE; an injected call that succeeded → returns nothing.

## Docs
One short sentence each in `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, and `USAGE.md`, in the most fitting existing section (safety/limits or subagent behavior): in print/json runs and subagent/workflow child sessions, bash calls without a `timeout` get a 120-second default; interactive sessions keep Pi's behavior (no default). Run the docs/config contract checks that `bun run check` includes.

## Verification (required)
- Before any manual Pi smoke, follow CONTRIBUTING.md section "Development runtime: npm vs current source": prove the checkout revision and that `pi list` reports this checkout as the single OpenPI source; if the installed OpenPI is the npm package rather than this checkout, run the smoke with this checkout loaded the documented way. If you cannot make it load the checkout, stop and report.
- Confirm the Web workbench (`extensions/web`) does not host its sessions in `print`/`json` mode (it should be rpc or its own host). If it does use print/json, stop and report before committing — that would wrongly apply the limit to interactive Web sessions.
- Real smoke 1 (print mode, uses the user's configured default model — one short prompt): `pi -p "Use the bash tool exactly once, without a timeout argument, to run: sleep 125; echo done. Then report the tool result verbatim."` Expect the bash result to be a timeout after 120 s with the NOTE appended. Capture the session JSONL path and the relevant toolResult text.
- Real smoke 2 (child session): `pi -p "Spawn one subagent with subagent_spawn whose task is: use bash once, without a timeout argument, to run sleep 125; echo done, and report the result verbatim. Then call subagent_wait and report what the subagent returned."` Expect the child's bash to time out at 120 s with the NOTE. Capture evidence (child session file or the delivered result text).
  Run the two smokes in parallel in the background if convenient.
- `bun run check` and `bun run test` must pass.

## Report back
Branch + commit sha, full `git diff main --stat`, the test file paths, check/test summaries, both smoke evidence excerpts (paths + the toolResult text), and the Web-mode finding. Leave no background processes running.

### Assistant

**Stopping per the handoff's gate — the Web workbench does bind `mode: "print"`.** Here is the verified evidence chain:

## Finding

`web/runtime/pi-runtime.ts:2654`:
```ts
await session.bindExtensions({ mode: "print", onError: (error) => {
  publishWebCommandFeedback(session.sessionManager, error.error, "error");
} });
```
This is the only `bindExtensions` path for Web sessions — called from `initializeRuntimeSession` (line 2625) and every `setRebindSession` replacement (line 2628).

**No `uiContext` is passed anywhere in `web/`** (grep for `uiContext` in `web/`: zero hits). Tracing Pi internals:
- `agent-session.js:2630-2645`: `bindExtensions` without `uiContext` leaves `_extensionUIContext` undefined → `runner.setUIContext(undefined, "print")` (line 2694)
- `runner.js:355-356`: `setUIContext(uiContext, mode)` → `this.uiContext = uiContext ? … : noOpUIContext`
- `runner.js:404-405`: `hasUI() { return this.uiContext !== noOpUIContext }` → **false**

So at a `tool_call` hook, a **Web workbench session presents `ctx = { mode: "print", hasUI: false }` — indistinguishable from a real `pi -p` run** and from a subagent/workflow child (`extensions/shared/child-session.ts:809` binds `{ mode: "print" }` with no uiContext either). There is **no ctx-level discriminator** between "the process exits after this turn" and "a human is driving an interactive Web session". `hasUI` doesn't help (false for both); `ExtensionMode` is a closed union (`"tui" | "rpc" | "json" | "print"`), so "web" isn't a legal label.

Consequence: the settled gate `ctx.mode === "print" || ctx.mode === "json"` would inject the 120 s default into **every interactive Web session's** timeout-less bash call — the wrongly-applied case you told me to stop on.

**Same root cause also affects merged code**: `subagent_spawn`'s `exitsAfterTurn` (commit a055ca77, merged via #880) uses the identical gate, so Web sessions already get "the process exits when your turn ends" guidance — false, since the Web host stays alive and auto-delivers. Minor, but worth knowing.

## Options (not picked — your call)

1. **Web declares `mode: "rpc"`** — one-line change at pi-runtime.ts:2654. Semantically defensible (Web is a programmatic host driving sessions over its own protocol, like RPC mode). `hasUI` stays false, so every `ctx.mode !== "tui"` guard still bails correctly (grep: all OpenPI mode checks are `!== "tui"`/`=== "tui"` plus the two `print|json` gates — no extension checks `=== "rpc"` positively; Pi only stores the label on the runner). Fixes both the new bash-timeout *and* the existing `exitsAfterTurn` misguidance for Web.
2. **Apply the timeout to Web too** — arguably also correct (a hung bash can't be Esc'd there either; the user does have a stop button that aborts the whole run). Then the gate stays as designed and I document that print-mode includes Web sessions.
3. Any other discriminator you'd like (e.g., a marker binding through `bindExtensions` — Pi supports arbitrary extra bindings fields? — or a Web-specific extension exclusion at `createChildResources`-style filtering).

Repo state: `feat/noninteractive-bash-timeout` branch created off `main@49b2ca34`, clean tree, nothing written yet, nothing committed, no background processes. Waiting for direction — option 1 looks cleanest to me but it changes Web's declared mode, which is above this task's scope without your sign-off.

## User

<lead_handoff>
Decision: take option 1. The Web workbench is a long-lived programmatic host, not a run that exits after its turn, so it should declare `mode: "rpc"`. I verified: Pi core only stores the mode label (no branching in dist/core); no installed third-party extension (pi-web-access, pi-intercom) reads ctx.mode; OpenPI's checks are all `tui` comparisons plus the two `print|json` gates; Web already steers with `source: "rpc"` (pi-runtime.ts:1719,1725). Fixing it at the shared bind point also corrects the merged `exitsAfterTurn` guidance for Web sessions.

Do this on the same branch `feat/noninteractive-bash-timeout`, as TWO commits:
1. `fix(web): bind Web sessions as rpc, not print` — change `web/runtime/pi-runtime.ts:2654` to `mode: "rpc"` (and any typed helper/test double that pins "print" for Web). Add/adjust one focused test that asserts Web binds with `mode: "rpc"` (find the existing Web runtime test that fakes `bindExtensions`; extend it rather than creating new infrastructure). Also confirm via an existing or one new small subagents test that `exitsAfterTurn` is false for `rpc` (only add it if no existing test already covers a non-print mode). Commit message body: Web hosts stay alive and auto-deliver subagent results, so print mode wrongly told the model the process exits after its turn; rpc keeps hasUI false so every tui-guarded path is unchanged.
2. The bash-timeout extension exactly as specified in my previous handoff (design, NOTE text, tests, docs, wiring), with the gate `ctx.mode === "print" || ctx.mode === "json"` unchanged. In the docs sentence, interactive = terminal (tui) and the Web workbench.

 "content": "/**\n * Non-interactive runs cannot be interrupted: nobody presses Esc in\n * `pi -p`/`--mode json` or in a subagent/workflow child session, so an\n * unbounded bash command can hang until the outer deadline kills everything.\n * Give bash a bounded default there. Interactive (tui) and rpc sessions keep\n * Pi's native behavior — no default timeout.\n */\n\nimport type { ExtensionAPI } from \"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent\";\n\nexport const DEFAULT_BASH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120;\n\nexport const BASH_TIMEOUT_NOTE = `OpenPI applied its default ${DEFAULT_BASH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}-second limit because this non-interactive run called bash without a timeout. If the command legitimately needs longer, run it again with a larger timeout (in seconds); start long-running services in the background with nohup … &.`;\n\nexport default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) {\n  const injected = new Set<string>();\n\n  pi.on(\"tool_call\", (event, ctx) => {\n    if (event.toolName !== \"bash\") return;\n    if (ctx.mode !== \"print\" && ctx.mode !== \"json\") return;\n    if (event.input.timeout !== undefined) return;\n    event.input.timeout = DEFAULT_BASH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS;\n    injected.add(event.toolCallId);\n  });\n\n  pi.on(\"tool_result\", (event) => {\n    if (!injected.delete(event.toolCallId)) return;\n    const timedOut =\n      event.isError &&\n      event.content.some(\n        (part) =>\n          part.type === \"text\" &&\n          part.text.includes(\n            `Command timed out after ${DEFAULT_BASH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS} seconds`,\n          ),\n      );\n    if (!timedOut) return;\n    return {\n      content: [\n        ...event.content,\n        { type: \"text\" as const, text: BASH_TIMEOUT_NOTE },\n      ],\n    };\n  });\n}\n"
}

## Goal
Show each subagent's cumulative token spend (and cost when known) to the user, and in subagent_check. Today the snapshot only carries context occupancy (`usage: {tokens, contextWindow}` in `extensions/subagents/src/domain.ts:255`), so nobody can see what a child consumed. Workflows already track per-agent usage (`extensions/workflows/model.ts` `AgentUsage`); this brings subagents to parity. Do NOT change the model-visible content of delivered subagent results, and do not add result size caps (outputs are already bounded at 24 KB with artifact spill).

## Settled design
1. `domain.ts`: add
   `export interface SubagentSpend { readonly input: number; readonly output: number; readonly cacheRead: number; readonly cacheWrite: number; readonly cost: number }`
   Extend the `UsageChanged` event with optional `spend?: SubagentSpend`, and `SubagentSnapshot` with optional `spend?: SubagentSpend`. Keep the existing `usage` (context occupancy) untouched.
2. `src/backends/pi.ts` `emitUsage` (line ~360): also read `session.getSessionStats()` (Pi `SessionStats`: `tokens.{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite}`, `cost`) and emit it as `spend`. Cumulative over the child session (a resumed child keeps accumulating — intended). Guard: if getSessionStats is unavailable/throws, omit spend (do not fail the run). Make sure emitUsage fires at least after each finalized assistant message and at settle (check where it is called today; add a call at settle if missing).
3. `src/manager.ts` UsageChanged fold: `s.spend = event.spend ?? s.spend`.
4. Formatter `formatSubagentSpend(spend?: SubagentSpend)` (put it next to `formatCompactTokens` in `extensions/shared/context-utilization.ts`, reuse that function): returns `undefined` when spend is absent or all token fields are 0; otherwise `"<in> in (<cached> cached) · <out> out"` where in = input + cacheRead + cacheWrite, cached = cacheRead, out = output, each via formatCompactTokens; append `" · $<cost>"` only when cost > 0, cost with 4 decimals below $1 and 2 decimals otherwise. Omit the `(… cached)` part when cacheRead is 0.
5. Surfaces:
   - `describeSubagent` (`extensions/subagents/index.ts:245`): add the formatted spend to the details list (after context utilization). This flows into subagent_check text.
   - TUI: wherever `formatContextUtilization(snap.usage)` is shown (`src/ui/takeover.ts` ~361 and ~450, `navigation.ts` ~166 list), show the spend string alongside, dim, without breaking existing width handling.
   - Delivered result: add `spend` to `SubagentResultDetails` (index.ts ~210–228) when building the result entry; the TUI custom-message renderer for subagent results shows one dim line with the formatted spend. The message `content` sent to the model stays exactly as today.
   - Web: add optional `spend` (the five numbers) to `WebSubagentDetail` (`extensions/shared/web-observer-registry.ts`), pass it in `projectSubagentDetail`, and render it in `web/ui/src/features/subagents/SubagentPanel.tsx` detail header next to model/context, using i18n keys in both locales (follow existing `t(...)` usage and locale files). Format on the Web side with the same rules (import the shared formatter if the UI already imports from `extensions/shared`, as SubagentPanel does for types; otherwise mirror it minimally).
6. No setup option, no new tool, no tool schema/description change (resident surface byte-identical).

## Tests (existing frameworks/locations, small)
- formatter: absent/zero → undefined; compact numbers; cached part omitted when 0; cost omitted when 0, 4 vs 2 decimals.
- manager: UsageChanged with spend updates snapshot; later event without spend keeps the previous spend.
- backend: a fake session whose getSessionStats returns known numbers → emitted UsageChanged carries them; a session whose getSessionStats throws → no spend, run continues.
- describeSubagent / subagent_check text includes the spend string.
- delivered result: details contain spend; model-facing content unchanged (assert equality with the pre-change builder output).
- Web projection includes spend; SubagentPanel renders it (follow the existing Web test style; update the subagent-inspection E2E only if it asserts header text that changes).
- Add a resident-surface guard only if one does not already exist that would fail on tool description changes (one likely exists — just make sure it still passes).

## Verification
- Runtime provenance per CONTRIBUTING.md before any manual smoke (`pi list` must show this checkout).
- Real smoke (print mode, use `--model bai/deepseek-v4.1-flash` since the user's default provider currently returns connection errors): `pi -p --model bai/deepseek-v4.1-flash "Spawn one subagent with subagent_spawn to list the files in the current directory with bash and report them. Call subagent_wait, then call subagent_check with that subagent's id and report the subagent_check text verbatim."` in a scratch dir under /tmp. Capture the subagent_check text showing the spend string, and the session JSONL path where the subagent-result entry's details contain spend.
- Web: run the subagent-related Web E2E specs locally (`bunx playwright test --config tests/web/playwright.config.ts` with the subagent/session specs you ran last time) and, if feasible, capture one screenshot of the SubagentPanel detail header showing spend (path in report).
- `bun run check` and `bun run test` must pass.

Report: commit sha(s), `git diff main --stat`, test paths, check/test/E2E summaries, smoke evidence (subagent_check text + JSONL path), screenshot path if captured. Leave no background processes.

# OpenPI agent contract

OpenPI is a Pi-native capability layer, not a second agent operating system. Extend Pi at its existing seams and preserve its lifecycle, vocabulary, and sources of truth.

## Design stance

### Build for model leverage

- Prefer capabilities whose usefulness increases as models improve.
- Give the model small, orthogonal mechanisms and high-fidelity feedback. Let the model decide strategy, decomposition, delegation, and synthesis.
- Encode safety and execution invariants in the runtime. Do not encode a preferred reasoning process, keyword router, or fixed orchestration workflow unless correctness requires it.
- Before adding a framework abstraction, ask whether a stronger model could use the underlying Pi primitive directly. If yes, expose or strengthen that primitive instead.

function deferred<T>() {
  let resolve!: (value: T) => void;
  let reject!: (reason?: unknown) => void;
  const promise = new Promise<T>((next, fail) => {
    resolve = next;

  });

async function waitFor(
  predicate: () => boolean,
  label: string,
  timeoutMs = 2_000,
) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    if (predicate()) return;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5));
  }
  assert.ok(predicate(), `timed out waiting for ${label}`);
}

## Diff — `git diff main --stat`

**20 files, +571/−34.** Highlights:

- **`src/domain.ts`**: `SubagentSpend {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, cost}` added; optional `spend` on `UsageChanged` and `SubagentSnapshot`. `usage` (context occupancy) untouched.
- **`src/backends/pi.ts`**: `emitUsage` reads `session.getSessionStats()` defensively (`try/catch` + optional call — never fails the run), emits `spend`, and `settle()` now calls `emitUsage()` for a final cumulative snapshot. Still fires after each finalized assistant message.
- **`src/manager.ts`**: `s.spend = event.spend ?? s.spend` — later usage events without spend keep the prior value.
- **`context-utilization.ts`**: `formatSubagentSpend` — `"<in> in (<cached> cached) · <out> out"` (in = input+cacheRead+cacheWrite via `formatCompactTokens`, cached part omitted when `cacheRead===0`), ` · $<cost>` only when >0 (4 decimals <$1, 2 otherwise), `undefined` when absent/all-zero.

## Goal
Child sessions (subagents AND workflow agents) must not load OpenPI's two orchestration skills, `skills/subagents/SKILL.md` and `skills/workflows/SKILL.md`. Children have no orchestration tools (they're in CHILD_EXCLUDED_TOOL_NAMES), yet their `<available_skills>` list advertises these two skills — confirmed in a benchmark child session that had only read/bash/edit/write. Parent sessions must be unchanged.

## Design (settled)
Use the existing seam in `extensions/shared/child-session.ts`: `disableOpenPiGitInfo(source)` (~line 431) already rewrites the OpenPI package source for children by appending the Pi package filter `-extensions/git-info/index.ts` (CHILD_DISABLED_OPENPI_EXTENSION). Extend that same rewrite to also append exclusion entries to the package source's `skills` filter for the two skills. Rename the function to reflect its broader role (e.g. `restrictOpenPiForChild`) and update callers. Mirror the existing early-return guards per-field: an explicit `skills: []` means already none → leave skills alone; `autoload:false` with `skills` undefined → none loaded → leave alone; don't duplicate an exclusion already present. Keep extension handling exactly as is.

Must verify (don't assume): the exact Pi package-filter syntax for skills — whether entries are skill directories (`-skills/subagents`) or SKILL.md files, relative to package root — by reading Pi's package manager source in the installed Pi (`~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, check `pi --version` matches what the repo pins/tests against). Also verify every path by which OpenPI is loaded into a child gets this (whatever paths the git-info exclusion already covers — package source in user/project settings, plus any temporary / `-e` / local-path load the git-info logic handles). If some load path can't be filtered the same way, stop and report rather than inventing a new mechanism. Confirm workflow agents go through the same child-session builder.

## Tests
Extend the existing child-session tests that cover the git-info exclusion (find them under tests/extensions/shared or similar). Assert, ideally through the real resource loader the way existing tests do: child loads neither orchestration skill; parent still loads both; a user's unrelated skill still loads in the child; the guard cases (skills: [], autoload false) are preserved; extension filter still contains git-info exclusion. Apply the test-value skill — a few focused cases, no snapshot churn.

## Verify
`bun run check`, the focused test files, then `bun run test` once at the end. Commit locally on a new branch `fix/child-skip-orchestration-skills` with a concise message (include the Devin generated/co-author trailer). Do NOT push. Report: diff summary, the Pi filter syntax you verified (with file:line in Pi), load paths covered, and test output counts.

## Diff summary

`extensions/shared/child-session.ts` (+100):
- `disableOpenPiGitInfo` → **`restrictOpenPiForChild`**: per-field guards now — `extensions:[]`/`autoload:false`+absent skips extension handling, `skills:[]`/`autoload:false`+absent skips skill handling, and returns early only when both are already disabled. Appends `-skills/subagents` and `-skills/workflows` to the package `skills` filter with dedup (mirrors `disablesOpenPiGitInfo`, tolerates `-./` prefix).
- **`resolveOrchestrationSkillDirsOrThrow`** + **`excludeOpenPiOrchestrationSkills`** — canonical-path post-filter on `Skill.baseDir`, same ENOENT-degrades/non-ENOENT-fail-closed contract as git-info, wired as `skillsOverride` in `createChildResources` next to the existing `extensionsOverride`.

## Verified facts (not assumed)

- **Pi filter syntax** (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.2.0`, matches `bun.lock`; installed `pi` binary is 1.3.0, satisfies `>=0.99.1`/`^1.2.0`): `-pattern` is a **force-exclude exact path** applied last in `applyPatterns` (`dist/core/package-manager.js:539-576`), and for `SKILL.md` files `matchesAnyExactPattern` also matches the **parent dir** (`package-manager.js:494-515`) — so `-skills/subagents` excludes `skills/subagents/SKILL.md`, relative to package root (`baseDir=packageRoot`, `applyPackageFilter` :1904). `skills:[]` disables all (`:1908`); `autoload:false` uses delta patterns (`applyPackageDeltaFilter` :1928).
- **Load paths**: `settings.packages` (user+project scope) → covered by the rewrite; auto-discovered `~/.agents/skills`, `agentDir/skills`, `cwd/.pi/skills` → covered by `skillsOverride` (a symlinked orchestration dir is the real-world case — `collectSkillEntries` follows symlinked dirs at `package-manager.js:233-243`). `settings.skills` entries are only enable/disable **patterns** over auto-discovered dirs, not load paths (verified `addAutoDiscoveredResources` :1985-2034) — nothing new to filter. Temporary `-e`/`-s` loads don't exist for SDK children (no `skillPaths` passed).
- **Workflow agents** go through the same `createChildResources` (`extensions/workflows/runner.ts:143`, same as subagents `backends/pi.ts:235`) — one fix covers both. `ResolvedPaths` dedupes skills by canonical path with user-auto beating package precedence (`toResolvedPaths` :2112-2135) — which is exactly why the post-filter is needed.
- `~/.agents/skills` on this machine contains no `subagents`/`workflows` skills — no environment contamination.
